hero.title: AI Agent Workspace for Studios and Agencies
hero.description: Keep briefs, research, production files, specialist work, feedback, approvals, and final delivery connected across the people and agents contributing to a client project.

burdens.title: A brief changes as it passes through the studio
burdens.description: Studios must preserve the client's intent while research, strategy, writing, design, production, and account review happen across different hands.

items.label: Brief
items.title: The approved brief is not the whole context
items.description: Calls, references, constraints, prior feedback, and unstated decisions often matter as much as the final brief document.

items.label: Handoff
items.title: Specialists receive different versions of truth
items.description: A writer, designer, producer, and account lead may each work from a different file, comment thread, or client interpretation.

items.label: Review
items.title: Feedback loses its target
items.description: Comments arrive through meetings, email, chat, and annotated files, sometimes after the underlying asset has already changed.

items.label: Delivery
items.title: Final packaging is still a project
items.description: Versions, formats, rights, naming, metadata, and client instructions must all be correct after the creative work is approved.

workflows.title: Preserve intent through every handoff
workflows.description: The workspace connects project evidence and production work while the project lead retains quality and client responsibility.

items.title: Turn a client brief into a production plan
items.job: Combine the approved brief, source material, constraints, references, and open questions before specialists begin work.
items.output: A production plan, source index, role-specific packets, and open-question list.
items.boundary: The project lead confirms interpretation, scope, staffing, timing, and what has client approval.

items.title: Coordinate a multi-specialist production run
items.job: Keep research, copy, design, media, and agent outputs tied to the current brief and dependencies.
items.output: A versioned asset set, dependency log, review notes, and unresolved decisions.
items.boundary: Humans direct the craft, resolve conflicts, and approve each discipline's work.

items.title: Prepare a client review and delivery pack
items.job: Consolidate approved assets, explanations, version notes, formats, and next questions for a clean client handoff.
items.output: A client review pack, delivery folder, version record, and follow-up brief.
items.boundary: The account or project lead approves claims, files, access, recipients, and release timing.

faq.title: Studio and agency AI workspace questions
faq.description: Studios need faster coordination without flattening specialist craft, confusing versions, or sending unapproved work to a client.

items.question: Is Floatboat a creative project-management system?
items.answer: No. Keep the system your studio uses for formal project tracking. Floatboat provides a working context for files, agents, handoffs, drafts, and deliverable preparation.

items.question: Can multiple agents replace studio specialists?
items.answer: Agents can split research and production steps, but specialists still direct the work, judge craft, resolve trade-offs, and approve what represents the studio.

items.question: How does it keep the brief consistent across disciplines?
items.answer: Use one approved context, role-specific instructions, explicit dependencies, and versioned review sets instead of copying the brief into separate unconnected chats.

items.question: Can each client have different workflows and standards?
items.answer: Yes. Templates, rights, naming, review stages, deliverable formats, and approval roles should be configured per client or project.

items.question: How should confidential client assets be handled?
items.answer: Apply contract and studio policy, isolate client work where needed, grant minimum access, and inspect the processing behavior of every model and connector.

items.question: Will deliverables be sent to the client automatically?
items.answer: The recommended workflow produces a review and delivery pack. A responsible project or account lead approves files, recipients, access, and timing before release.

items.question: What is the best first studio workflow?
items.answer: Choose one current project with a stable brief and two specialist handoffs. Test whether shared context reduces clarification and version errors before broadening the workflow.

finalCta.title: Keep the brief intact from kickoff to delivery
finalCta.description: Bring one approved brief, its source files, and the next specialist handoff. Build a clearer production thread before automating more of the studio.
